newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond mart sidelined after Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond mart sidelined after Greenspan.

text.p: Inflation warnings by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan sparked a sharp selloff in U.S. Treasury and stock markets and sidelined corporate high-grade and junk bond players on Wednesday, traders said.
"It's very quiet. Any time the Treasury market moves as much as this its hard to trade a lot," one high-grade trader said.

Treasuries and stocks slid following Greenspan's warning that financial markets, including stock and junk bond prices, may be overly optimistic about the economy, and urged caution during his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony earlier in the day.
The 30-year T-bond sold off over a point immediately after his comments to end the day off 48/32 at 98-3/32 to yield 6.77 percent, compared with Tuesday's 6.65 percent at the close.
In the high-grade sector, spreads to U.S. Treasuries remained unchanged across the board as players sat out the afternoon trading session amid the volatility but better buying was seen.

"We had a quiet afternoon...most people got their business done early before the market fell out of bed," said one high-grade trader. "Then we saw some pretty decent buying coming in particularly from insurance companies."
High-yield prices were unchanged to off 1/4 point despite volatility in other financial markets, traders said. Spreads actually tightened as a result of the dramatic rise in Treasury yields.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended off 55 points on the day at 6983.18, after a volatile trading session.

In testimony given to members of the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday morning, Greenspan delivered an upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy but voiced concerns about soaring prices in the financial markets.
In his testimony, Greenspan said, "Caution also seems warranted by the narrow yield spreads that suggest perceptions of low risk, possibly unrealistically low risk."
He said optimism about business activity "has become especially evident in quality spreads on high-yield corporate bonds - what we use to call junk bonds."

Players noted, however, that spreads on high-yield bonds have reached historically tight levels in recent weeks, propelled by positive views on the economy as well as tremendous cash inflows into high-yield mutual funds.
"There;s still too much money on the sidelines...investors are looking to buy paper," said one high-yield trader.
"You get these little murmours and people step back for a bit but essentially they still have to put money to work, so until the faucet gets turned off you're going to find support levels," he added.

Meanwhile, Marvel Entertainment parent companies' debt forged about two point gains on Wednesday after a U.S bankruptcy judge on Tuesday said bondholders had the right to foreclose on the stock that backs the bonds.
Marvel Holding's "old" bonds were quoted at 19-1/2 on Wednesday afternoon compared with 17-1/4 market on Tuesday.
Marvel (Parent) holdings "new" bonds were offered at 16.
The bonds have traded below 20 since Marvel and its holding companies filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on December 27.
Elsewhere, Penn Traffic 9.625 percent bonds slid about three points to a 43-1/2 bid, 48 offer, while Pioneer Finance bonds gained three points to trade at a 73 bid, 76 offer, traders added.
((--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675))
